ai.description: *Leptobrachella khasiorum* is a small frog (22–26 mm) with a brown dorsum featuring dark, irregular markings. It is distinguished by a white-spotted venter and a distinct, rounded snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Leptobrachella khasiorum* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, small, rounded, creamy-white tubercles scattered across its dorsal surface.
ai.habitat: *Leptobrachella khasiorum* inhabits moist, evergreen broadleaf forests in the Khasi Hills, typically found near rocky, fast-flowing streams at elevations between 800–1,500m.
ai.behavior: *Leptobrachella khasiorum* is primarily nocturnal, remaining active at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky, mossy banks of fast-flowing forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Leptobrachella khasiorum* breeds in streams during the monsoon (May–August). Females lay small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs attached to submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Leptobrachella khasiorum* is endemic to the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, India, where it inhabits high-elevation evergreen forests between 1,000 and 1,900 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Leptobrachella khasiorum* consists of a series of high-pitched, pulsed notes emitted by individuals perched near fast-flowing forest streams.
